The finale of Succession left me with so many emotions. The Roy family saga's conclusion was intense and full of the unexpected twists that have kept us hooked from the beginning. Kendall's journey was a rollercoaster, and Jeremy Strong delivered a performance that embodied every complex layer of his character. Roman, played brilliantly by Kieran Culkin, had moments that were both heart-wrenching and absurdly humorous, showing just how fragile these characters are despite their massive power. 

Shiv's path was another fascinating thread, with Sarah Snook capturing her inner conflicts so vividly. The dynamic between her and Tom, with Matthew Macfadyen bringing surprising depth to his role, highlighted just how complicated relationships can become when power is at play. 

And of course, Brian Cox as Logan Roy was the force that held it all together, even as his presence became more shadow than substance in the family's lives. I'm left pondering their legacy and wondering if the next generation truly stands any chance of escaping the cycle. What a ride this show has been!

drafts.content: Having just finished 'In the Mood for Love,' I'm left pondering the subtle art of what isn't said. How they navigate their circumstances, never quite stepping over the line, makes for such a poignant experience. I wonder if their story would resonate the same today, or if our digital age would rob it of its nuance. Can modern relationships still afford that kind of narrative mystery?
